Persona 4 is one of the most heartwarming games I’ve ever played. I’m not surprised it has a cult status. If you enjoy a captivating story, well written characters, and beautiful art design - 100% recommend it. Don’t let the old graphics bother you, trust me, you’ll be so immersed in the story that you won’t even notice! At this moment - it’s the best game I’ve played on the Steam Deck!

Definitely one of the best games i've ever played. Had a total of 4 playthroughs where i was able to experience many different interactions, the endings and eventually finding a more optimal route to complete the game.

It's the first of the Persona games i play. At first, i was trying to speed through it but that turned out to be a gigantic mistake. It is by taking your time during dialogue, during cutscenes and having a bit of patience with the dungeons that you truly come to bond with the game and its characters. This is one of those games that make you WISH you could play it for the first time again the most. The first time you play through this game is an absolutely amazing experiences with engaging story elements carefully put together and neat details.

There are MANY, MANY things you can do to progress through the story which enables the player great flexibility when it comes to creating your route. Most of the time, you'll spend time with other people, but you must not forget yourself and your own stats.

Even after a second full playthrough, Persona 4 Golden never stopped being enjoyable to me. The story, characters, social links and soundtracks are just as engaging the second time as they were during my first playthrough. Instead of feeling like a grind, going for the 100% completion just gave me even more appreciation for the game. There's only been a few games that can make me invested for more than 50+ hours of gameplay but P4G managed to do exactly that. It's still a peak game for me and I'm glad it was my first introduction to the series 💛

Persona 4 is a turn-based party JRPG/visual novel adventure game hybrid, where the main character forms his band of detectives to unravel a meandering murder mystery, with twists and surprise reveals at every turn, In between dungeon delving and monster (persona) collecting are entertaining slice-of-life segments in a high school/college setting, though JRPG and anime fanatics might find some of the scenes very tropey and familiar. The undoubted star of the show is the diverse ensemble of characters, each with their own unique personalities and backstories. Coupled with the excellent soundtrack and art style, this timeless JRPG classic is still immensely enjoyable despite being a decade old. You will easily spend 50-80 hours to play through the story. For min-maxers and tactics JRPG die-hards, many more hundreds of hours beckon.

Only 2 dungeons in but so far so good. I played Persona 5 before this, so I automatically compare the two games. This is def a more rudimentary version of that game but still immensely fun in its own right.

At core it is social simulation + turn-based battler, same as Persona 5. Both parts are fine but not as polished as P5R. Story is very comparable, you go to another realm to figure out what the hell is going on in a mystical/unconscious plane that is affecting physical world.

I'd say if you enjoy JRPGs or turn-based combat in general you'd like this.

8.5/10 rating

Persona 4 is my favorite in the series next to Persona 2 (dont really like the others).
This one has a more light hearted pop tone (which contrasts great against the murder story).

The plot moves around the little rural town of Inaba; you have to keep a social and anime demon fighting life balance, the relationships you improve on the social aspect will help you on the RPG aspect as every mechanic is connected to another.

This is one of my favorite games, not my favorite Shin Megami Tensei, but in general terms it just feels so good in every aspect.

It also has probably the best character development of the series, without a doubt better than P3 or P5

I really enjoyed this game, the characters and story were great. Sometimes the dungeons could drag on a bit, but they were easy enough on the easiest difficulty, which I'm grateful for. Easy actually felt easy and I could just enjoy the story without having to worry too much about grinding or maximising skills or anything.

I really liked the time aspect in having to choose who to hang out with and what activities to do, it was very engaging and fun to see all of the interaction and scenes. I was able to see the Golden Ending by following a simple guide reminding me to level certain Social Links before a certain point.

I was able to finish the game spoiler-free doing this and saw mostly everything I wanted to see in a single playthrough, but obviously not all. I'll definitely return for a newgame+ several years in the future.

I look forward to playing Persona 5 Royal next.

Although judging by previous Persona titles, this doesn't seem to be a game series to pick up on release, since they make a habit of re-releasing definitive versions with extra content.
